192	  You are connected to an MCP Context Server at http://LAB-OMARCHY:7147. Use this server to coordinate your work.
193	
194	  ## Session Start (Run Once Per Session)
195	  1. Read this marker file for connection details and API key.
196	  2. Bootstrap the required plugin named for your agent in the top-level `agent_plugins` contract. Get the plugin through the MCP Server tool registry before relying on local root hints: search `/mcpserver/tools/search?keyword=<plugin_name>` for the installed tool definition and select the result whose `name` exactly equals `<plugin_name>`; if that exact tool definition is missing, install the definition from `/mcpserver/tools/buckets/official/install?toolName=<plugin_name>`, then search again. Execute the exact tool definition's returned `commandTemplate` with `targetParent` set to the plugin parent directory to clone or update the plugin repository. Codex must use `mcpserver-codex-plugin`; Claude must use `mcpserver-claude-code-plugin`; Copilot must use `mcpserver-copilot-plugin`; Cline must use `mcpserver-cline-plugin`; Grok must use `mcpserver-grok-plugin`.
197	  3. Verify the marker signature using the workspace API key in this file before contacting the server.
198	  4. Call /health with a random nonce and confirm the response echoes that exact nonce.
199	  5. Verify and log plugin identity before other MCP work: sourceType, plugin name/version, plugin root or MCP server name, marker signature result, health nonce result, and workspace path.
200	  6. Review recent session history and current TODOs only after signature, nonce, and plugin verification succeed.
201	  7. Post an initial session log turn for the session.

203	  ## Required Agent Plugins
204	  - `agent_plugins.policy` is `required`. The plugin contract or deterministic digest is covered by marker signature verification. - Plugin acquisition is the bootstrap exception to the normal plugin-only rule: if the matching plugin is not already available locally, use the authenticated tool registry endpoints in this marker to locate/install the matching `mcpserver-*-plugin` tool definition from the `official` bucket and run its clone/update command. After acquisition, bootstrap and use the matching plugin for normal MCP work. - If your matching plugin cannot be acquired through the tool registry or remains unavailable after acquisition, stop MCP usage, record `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE:<Agent>`, and continue only with non-MCP local diagnosis. - Do not substitute raw REST, generic `mcpserver-repl`, helper modules, or another agent's plugin for normal session, TODO, requirements, import/export, or traceability operations. - Another agent's plugin may be inspected only for read-only diagnosis of plugin installation or contract drift. - Normal workspace shell commands use `pwsh.exe`. Plugin-owned hooks may use the runner declared by that plugin contract. - Codex plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Codex`; Claude plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Claude`; Copilot plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Copilot`; Cline MCP tools must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Cline`; Grok plugin skills/hooks/MCP server declarations must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Grok`. - For Grok, the Streamable HTTP MCP server exposes tool names such as `sessionlog_*`, `todo_*`, `requirements_*`, and memory tools when available; hosted-agent `mcp_*` names are not expected from that transport. `workflow.sessionlog.*`, `workflow.todo.*`, `workflow.memory.*`, and `workflow.requirements.*` are plugin shim/REPL method names used by the Grok skills and `repl-invoke` helpers; they are not expected to appear as literal `search_tool` results. - Local plugin root hints in `agent_plugins.agents.<Agent>.root_hints` are fallback verification hints after tool-registry acquisition, not the primary install source. - Claude Code agents must trigger the `claude-hook-validation` skill during marker/plugin bootstrap. That skill validates active Claude settings for MCP `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, and `PostToolUse` hook commands from `hooks/hooks.json`; if any required hook is missing, it uses `install-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1` from the `claude-hook-wiring` skill to merge MCP hooks into active Claude settings without replacing existing hooks. Restart Claude Code after the skill reports installed hooks.
205	
206	  ## Model-Authored Session Logging
207	  - Models must write MCP Session Log turns, dialog, actions, decisions, and completions themselves through the active agent's session-log surface (`workflow.sessionlog.*`, `sessionlog_*`, `mcp_session_*`, or equivalent plugin tool).
208	  - Plugins must not ingest local chat transcripts to populate normal session logs and must not expose transcript-ingestion helpers, skills, endpoint shortcuts, or parser forks.
209	  - Transcript ingestion and normalization are explicit non-plugin server/client/REPL/MCP operations. Use them only when the user asks to import or normalize transcript files, not as a substitute for live model-authored logging.
210	  ## MCP Requirements Visibility
211	  - When implementing or enforcing requirements, query current effective requirements for the active workspace layer through the active agent's requirements surface (`workflow.requirements.effective`, `client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`, `req_effective`, or equivalent plugin tool). Use the layer catalog surface (`workflow.requirements.listLayers/createLayer/updateLayer`, `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync/CreateRequirementLayerAsync/UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`, `req_list_layers/req_create_layer/req_update_layer`, or equivalent plugin tools) when the user asks to inspect or manage requirement layers. Do not treat raw all-requirements lists, exported markdown, or future-layer requirements as currently enforceable unless the user explicitly asks to inspect or plan those layers.
212	  ## YAML Mutation Rule
213	
214	  - Never edit YAML files by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. This includes one-key configuration changes.
215	
216	  - Always deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save the serialized result.
217	
218	  - For PowerShell work, use `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` and call `Set-McpYamlObjectValue` or `Update-McpYamlObject`. Do not build YAML snippets as strings or use line-oriented edit helpers for YAML.
219	
220	  ## MCP and Plugin Failure Reporting
221	  - MCP Server failures and required-plugin failures discovered while working must always be written as a normal failsafe YAML report. Use the plugin/REPL failsafe or pending YAML queue and preserve the triage method (`workflow.triage.report`, `triage_report`, or equivalent plugin triage tool) plus title, summary, observed behavior, expected behavior, severity, component, workspace path, dedupe key or error signature, affected paths, evidence, reproduction hints, tags, reporter agent, session id, turn id, and current TODO id when known.
222	  - After the failsafe YAML is written and triage submission succeeds, continue the user's active task. Do not wait for triage research, TODO creation, or resolution.
223	  - Do not create TODOs, requirements, GitHub issues, manual repair plans, or alternate reports for MCP Server/plugin failures unless the user's active request is to fix that failure.
224	  - If the MCP Server or required-plugin failure reveals that code, docs, requirements, plugin skills, package sync, deployment, configuration, or other artifacts need to be updated as a separate repair workflow, write a detailed triage report that includes the needed changes, acceptance criteria, and validation evidence, then continue the active task after the failsafe YAML is written and triage submission succeeds.
225	  - If triage submission fails, stop work and notify the user. Keep the failsafe YAML report for later replay; do not use raw REST or another reporting channel as a substitute.
226	
227	  ## Agent Help (MCP Server issues)
228	  When you are stuck on any MCP Server surface (marker trust, plugin bootstrap, session log, TODO, requirements, triage, memory, context search, federation, hooks, or API behavior), request expert help instead of improvising raw REST bypasses.
229	  - **When to invoke:** signature or health nonce failures you cannot resolve; unexpected tool or plugin behavior; `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE`; repeated 401/503 after re-reading this marker; documentation contradictions.
230	  - **How to invoke:** preferred `workflow.agenthelp.createSession` or MCP tool `agent_help_create_session` with caller linkage (`callerAgent`, `callerSessionId`, `callerRequestId`) and a factual issue summary (observation vs inference separated). REST: `POST /mcpserver/agent-help/session` then WebSocket `/mcpserver/agent-help/session/{id}/stream` (SSE fallback: `POST .../turn/stream`).
231	  - **Caller obligations:** include reproduction steps, exact error text, and files already consulted. Do not instruct the helper to ignore guardrails, skip triage, or mutate TODO/session-log/requirements storage directly.
232	  - Agent help is for diagnosis and coordination, not a substitute for the required plugin route for normal MCP work.
233	
234	  ## MCP Memories
235	  MCP memories are durable operator guidance managed by the MCP Server. Global memories apply to every workspace; Workspace memories apply only to the active workspace. Memory IDs use `MEMORY-{CATEGORY}-{NNN}`.
236	  Agents that support request-boundary injection must render required memories exactly as:
237	  REQUIRED MEMORIES - MEMORY-REQ-001: Raw memory text.
238	  If no required memories are visible, render:
239	  REQUIRED MEMORIES - None.
240	  Preserve raw memory text exactly; do not summarize, paraphrase, reorder within a scope, silently generate new memories, or add secrets. MCP memories are not a secret store. Effective memory order is Global memories first sorted by ID, then current Workspace memories sorted by ID.
241	  Existing agent-local memory stores are caches or migration sources only; the MCP memory store is the authoritative shared record. Import agent-local memories only when the operator approves the scope, the content belongs to this workspace or is intentionally Global, and the import does not leak secrets, private notes, or unrelated workspace guidance.
242	  Attribute memory mutations with the real agent or user identity via `updatedBy` when supported, and record successful memory add/update/remove operations in the active session log through `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`. Keep import provenance in the session log or dialog instead of adding private source paths to memory text.
243	  Manage memories through the required plugin or MCP tool surface: `memory_add`, `memory_list`, `memory_update`, `memory_remove`, `memory_remember`, `memory_recall`, `memory_explore`, `memory_consolidate`, `memory_promote`, `memory_revert`; REPL `workflow.memory.add`, `workflow.memory.list`, `workflow.memory.update`, `workflow.memory.remove`, `workflow.memory.remember`, `workflow.memory.recall`, `workflow.memory.explore`, `workflow.memory.consolidate`, `workflow.memory.promote`, `workflow.memory.revert`; or REST `/mcpserver/memory` when explicitly allowed for non-plugin diagnostics.
244	
245	  ## Codex MCP Quickstart
246	  If you are Codex, use the Codex plugin wrappers before direct REPL calls:
247	  1. Run `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status` from the `mcpserver-codex-plugin` root to verify plugin root, marker trust, health nonce, workspace path, session id, current turn, and supported namespaces.
248	  2. Invoke MCP workflow methods with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -Params <yaml>` so YAML parameters are passed through stdin instead of fragile nested shell quoting.
249	  3. Complete the session-log turn intentionally with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command CompleteTurn -Response <final response>` before the final answer when the stop gate cannot infer completion.
250	  4. For `mcpserver-repl --agent-stdio`, send one single-line JSON request envelope per stdin line. Do not send formatted YAML or a single `type: batch` envelope; batch envelopes are rejected with `unsupported_batch_envelope`.
251	
252	  ## PowerShell.MCP Command Routing
253	  For every PowerShell Core (`pwsh`) invocation on every operating system:
254	  - Use PowerShell.MCP 1.14.0 or newer from PSGallery as the command runner. Install or update it with `Install-PSResource PowerShell.MCP` when the agent environment does not provide a current version.
255	  - `execute_command` is the primary MCP tool for PowerShell cmdlets, CLI tools, navigation, builds, tests, file-system work, and process management. Do not use the removed `invoke_expression` name. Host-qualified names depend on the configured server key: for example, `mcp__powershell__execute_command` for `powershell` and `mcp__pwsh__execute_command` for `pwsh`.
256	  - Calling `start_console` first is optional because `execute_command` auto-starts or reuses a console. Call `start_console` explicitly only to pre-warm at `start_location`, show a banner, allocate a sub-agent console, or force an additional console by supplying `reason`; omit `reason` when reuse is preferred.
257	  - Use `get_current_location` when the current PowerShell context matters. For a sub-agent, call `start_console` with `is_subagent=true`, retain the returned `agent_id`, and pass it on every later PowerShell.MCP tool call.
258	  - When a command continues after the call returns, use `wait_for_completion` to retrieve the cached result instead of running `Start-Sleep`. Use `cancel` for an interruptible pipeline or native CLI, and `close_console` for a non-interruptible command or PowerShell host prompt. If `close_console` reports that a human is typing, only repeat the same PID call when confirming that the console should be closed.
259	  - In 1.14.0, blocking timeouts are end-to-end deadlines and are capped at 170 seconds for Claude Code and 50 seconds for other or unidentified clients unless a lower limit applies. A timed-out command keeps running and its result is cached for a later tool call.
260	  - Route `pwsh` commands through a PowerShell.MCP session instead of launching ad hoc PowerShell processes. On Windows, reuse one session for the workspace and route `node` invocations through it as well.
261	  - When PowerShell.MCP must launch PowerShell Core directly, invoke `pwsh.exe` with `-NoProfile -NonInteractive`. Do not use `powershell.exe`.
262	  - The PowerShell escape character is the backtick `` ` ``, not the backslash. Never use C or bash-style `\"` escaping inside PowerShell command strings.
263	  - Prefer single-quoted PowerShell strings for literal regex, paths, JSON/YAML snippets, and text containing pipeline characters such as `|`.
264	  - When a command needs nested quoting, choose one of these patterns before improvising: `-File` with explicit arguments; piping stdin to the called tool or script; single-quoted or double-quoted here-strings; `-EncodedCommand` for complex inline PowerShell; or correct backtick escaping for embedded PowerShell quotes.
265	  - If a regex or literal argument contains `|`, `&`, `;`, parentheses, braces, or quotes, verify it is inside a single PowerShell argument before running.
266	  - For text reads and edits inside PowerShell.MCP, use `Show-TextFiles`, `Add-LinesToFile`, `Update-LinesInFile`, `Update-MatchInFile`, and `Remove-LinesFromFile`; pass literal content through `var1` to `var4`. Version 1.12.0 and newer stage replacements beside the target, so do not apply the obsolete same-volume `TEMP`/`TMP` workaround. Re-read or diff every edit before claiming it landed.

270	  ## Federation Topology
271	  - To identify hub/proxy topology, call the supported federation status surface, preferably through your required plugin or client wrapper: `/mcpserver/federation/status`. - Status fields to report when relevant: `role`, `configuredRole`, `hubBaseUrl`, `proxyId`, `proxyCount`, `hostedWorkspaceCount`, `queueDepth`, `fanoutDepth`, `conflictCount`, and `staleReadStatus`. - `Standalone` serves local workspaces only. `DirectProxy` is the existing point-to-point proxy mode. `Hub` is authoritative for enrolled proxies and global workspace inventory. `LocalProxy` forwards MCP requests to `hubBaseUrl` and queues mutating requests during hub outages. - LocalProxy queued writes return `202 Accepted` with `X-Mcp-Queued: true` and `X-Mcp-Operation-Id`. Treat the write as optimistic until the hub acknowledges it. - If `queueDepth`, `fanoutDepth`, `conflictCount`, or stale-read status is non-zero/non-clear, include that in session log status and avoid claiming federation synchronization is complete.

273	  ## Per User Message
274	  1. Post a new session log turn before starting work.
275	  2. Complete the user's request.
276	  3. Update the turn with results and actions when done.

278	  ## Re-run Full Session Start Only If
279	  - The user explicitly says "Start Session". - Signature verification fails. - /health fails. - /health nonce verification fails. - Any /mcpserver/* call returns 401. - The marker endpoint/key changes after a server restart.
280	
281	  ## Continuing After a Server Restart
282	  The workspace API key rotates on every server restart, so an in-flight agent will begin seeing 401 on /mcpserver/* calls. When that happens, resume through your required agent plugin - do not hand-roll raw REST for session, TODO, or requirements work:
283	  1. Treat the first 401 (or a /health failure) as a restart signal and stop using the cached API key immediately.
284	  2. Re-read this marker file (AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml) for the rotated apiKey and current endpoints.
285	  3. Re-verify trust before resuming: recompute the marker signature with the new key and call /health with a fresh nonce.
286	  4. Re-bootstrap and resume through your required agent plugin. Codex: run `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status` to re-establish marker trust, health nonce, workspace, and the current session/turn, then continue with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -Params <yaml>`. Other agents: re-run the plugin session-start hook/command, then continue via the plugin session tools.
287	  5. Recover the open turn instead of starting over: query session history through the plugin (workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory), find the in-progress turn, then keep updating and complete it via the plugin. Do not open a duplicate session for the same work.
288	  5a. Treat `deprecated: true` on successful `workflow.*` results as metadata, not wrapper failure. Treat an empty `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` result as a valid no-match result. Re-check the workspace current directory, explicit `agent` or `sourceType`, and plugin cache/session state through the wrapper; do not use raw REST merely because history is empty or marked deprecated.
289	  6. If the plugin cannot re-establish trust after the restart, record `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE:<Agent>` and continue with non-MCP local diagnosis only.
290	
291	  ## Rules
292	  0. NEVER write to TODO.yaml directly.
293	  1. Generate SessionId values using `session.init` (REPL) or `New-McpSessionLogSlug -Agent <SourceType> -Model <Model>` (PowerShell module), then create session logs with `session.new` (REPL) or `New-McpSessionLog -SessionId` (PowerShell). Do not handcraft SessionId values.
294	  1a. Agents must identify themselves accurately in session logs. `sourceType` and the SessionId `<Agent>` prefix must use the agent's real identity in Pascal-Case. Do not use lowercase forms, placeholders, or legacy aliases.
295	  2. Post a new session log turn (`session.turn.add` for REPL or `Add-McpSessionTurn` for PowerShell) before starting work. Update it with results (`Response`) and actions (`Add-McpAction` / `session.action.add`) when done. Persist after each meaningful update, not just at the end.
296	  2a. Before any compaction step, persist the current session log state. After compaction, update the session log again to record the compaction outcome and recovered context.

  You are connected to an MCP Context Server at http://LAB-OMARCHY:7147. Use this server to coordinate your work.

  ## Session Start (Run Once Per Session)
  1. Read this marker file for connection details and API key.
  2. Bootstrap the required plugin named for your agent in the top-level `agent_plugins` contract. Get the plugin through the MCP Server tool registry before relying on local root hints: search `/mcpserver/tools/search?keyword=<plugin_name>` for the installed tool definition and select the result whose `name` exactly equals `<plugin_name>`; if that exact tool definition is missing, install the definition from `/mcpserver/tools/buckets/official/install?toolName=<plugin_name>`, then search again. Execute the exact tool definition's returned `commandTemplate` with `targetParent` set to the plugin parent directory to clone or update the plugin repository. Codex must use `mcpserver-codex-plugin`; Claude must use `mcpserver-claude-code-plugin`; Copilot must use `mcpserver-copilot-plugin`; Cline must use `mcpserver-cline-plugin`; Grok must use `mcpserver-grok-plugin`.
  3. Verify the marker signature using the workspace API key in this file before contacting the server.
  4. Call /health with a random nonce and confirm the response echoes that exact nonce.
  5. Verify and log plugin identity before other MCP work: sourceType, plugin name/version, plugin root or MCP server name, marker signature result, health nonce result, and workspace path.
  6. Review recent session history and current TODOs only after signature, nonce, and plugin verification succeed.
  7. Post an initial session log turn for the session.

  ## Required Agent Plugins
  - `agent_plugins.policy` is `required`. The plugin contract or deterministic digest is covered by marker signature verification. - Plugin acquisition is the bootstrap exception to the normal plugin-only rule: if the matching plugin is not already available locally, use the authenticated tool registry endpoints in this marker to locate/install the matching `mcpserver-*-plugin` tool definition from the `official` bucket and run its clone/update command. After acquisition, bootstrap and use the matching plugin for normal MCP work. - If your matching plugin cannot be acquired through the tool registry or remains unavailable after acquisition, stop MCP usage, record `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE:<Agent>`, and continue only with non-MCP local diagnosis. - Do not substitute raw REST, generic `mcpserver-repl`, helper modules, or another agent's plugin for normal session, TODO, requirements, import/export, or traceability operations. - Another agent's plugin may be inspected only for read-only diagnosis of plugin installation or contract drift. - Normal workspace shell commands use `pwsh.exe`. Plugin-owned hooks may use the runner declared by that plugin contract. - Codex plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Codex`; Claude plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Claude`; Copilot plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Copilot`; Cline MCP tools must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Cline`; Grok plugin skills/hooks/MCP server declarations must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Grok`. - For Grok, the Streamable HTTP MCP server exposes tool names such as `sessionlog_*`, `todo_*`, `requirements_*`, and memory tools when available; hosted-agent `mcp_*` names are not expected from that transport. `workflow.sessionlog.*`, `workflow.todo.*`, `workflow.memory.*`, and `workflow.requirements.*` are plugin shim/REPL method names used by the Grok skills and `repl-invoke` helpers; they are not expected to appear as literal `search_tool` results. - Local plugin root hints in `agent_plugins.agents.<Agent>.root_hints` are fallback verification hints after tool-registry acquisition, not the primary install source. - Claude Code agents must trigger the `claude-hook-validation` skill during marker/plugin bootstrap. That skill validates active Claude settings for MCP `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, and `PostToolUse` hook commands from `hooks/hooks.json`; if any required hook is missing, it uses `install-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1` from the `claude-hook-wiring` skill to merge MCP hooks into active Claude settings without replacing existing hooks. Restart Claude Code after the skill reports installed hooks.

  ## Model-Authored Session Logging
  - Models must write MCP Session Log turns, dialog, actions, decisions, and completions themselves through the active agent's session-log surface (`workflow.sessionlog.*`, `sessionlog_*`, `mcp_session_*`, or equivalent plugin tool).
  - Plugins must not ingest local chat transcripts to populate normal session logs and must not expose transcript-ingestion helpers, skills, endpoint shortcuts, or parser forks.
  - Transcript ingestion and normalization are explicit non-plugin server/client/REPL/MCP operations. Use them only when the user asks to import or normalize transcript files, not as a substitute for live model-authored logging.
  ## MCP Requirements Visibility
  - When implementing or enforcing requirements, query current effective requirements for the active workspace layer through the active agent's requirements surface (`workflow.requirements.effective`, `client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`, `req_effective`, or equivalent plugin tool). Use the layer catalog surface (`workflow.requirements.listLayers/createLayer/updateLayer`, `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync/CreateRequirementLayerAsync/UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`, `req_list_layers/req_create_layer/req_update_layer`, or equivalent plugin tools) when the user asks to inspect or manage requirement layers. Do not treat raw all-requirements lists, exported markdown, or future-layer requirements as currently enforceable unless the user explicitly asks to inspect or plan those layers.
  ## YAML Mutation Rule

  - Never edit YAML files by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. This includes one-key configuration changes.

  - Always deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save the serialized result.

  - For PowerShell work, use `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` and call `Set-McpYamlObjectValue` or `Update-McpYamlObject`. Do not build YAML snippets as strings or use line-oriented edit helpers for YAML.

  ## MCP and Plugin Failure Reporting
  - MCP Server failures and required-plugin failures discovered while working must always be written as a normal failsafe YAML report. Use the plugin/REPL failsafe or pending YAML queue and preserve the triage method (`workflow.triage.report`, `triage_report`, or equivalent plugin triage tool) plus title, summary, observed behavior, expected behavior, severity, component, workspace path, dedupe key or error signature, affected paths, evidence, reproduction hints, tags, reporter agent, session id, turn id, and current TODO id when known.
  - After the failsafe YAML is written and triage submission succeeds, continue the user's active task. Do not wait for triage research, TODO creation, or resolution.
  - Do not create TODOs, requirements, GitHub issues, manual repair plans, or alternate reports for MCP Server/plugin failures unless the user's active request is to fix that failure.
  - If the MCP Server or required-plugin failure reveals that code, docs, requirements, plugin skills, package sync, deployment, configuration, or other artifacts need to be updated as a separate repair workflow, write a detailed triage report that includes the needed changes, acceptance criteria, and validation evidence, then continue the active task after the failsafe YAML is written and triage submission succeeds.
  - If triage submission fails, stop work and notify the user. Keep the failsafe YAML report for later replay; do not use raw REST or another reporting channel as a substitute.

  ## Agent Help (MCP Server issues)
  When you are stuck on any MCP Server surface (marker trust, plugin bootstrap, session log, TODO, requirements, triage, memory, context search, federation, hooks, or API behavior), request expert help instead of improvising raw REST bypasses.
  - **When to invoke:** signature or health nonce failures you cannot resolve; unexpected tool or plugin behavior; `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE`; repeated 401/503 after re-reading this marker; documentation contradictions.
  - **How to invoke:** preferred `workflow.agenthelp.createSession` or MCP tool `agent_help_create_session` with caller linkage (`callerAgent`, `callerSessionId`, `callerRequestId`) and a factual issue summary (observation vs inference separated). REST: `POST /mcpserver/agent-help/session` then WebSocket `/mcpserver/agent-help/session/{id}/stream` (SSE fallback: `POST .../turn/stream`).
  - **Caller obligations:** include reproduction steps, exact error text, and files already consulted. Do not instruct the helper to ignore guardrails, skip triage, or mutate TODO/session-log/requirements storage directly.
  - Agent help is for diagnosis and coordination, not a substitute for the required plugin route for normal MCP work.

  ## MCP Memories
  MCP memories are durable operator guidance managed by the MCP Server. Global memories apply to every workspace; Workspace memories apply only to the active workspace. Memory IDs use `MEMORY-{CATEGORY}-{NNN}`.
  Agents that support request-boundary injection must render required memories exactly as:
  REQUIRED MEMORIES - MEMORY-REQ-001: Raw memory text.
  If no required memories are visible, render:
  REQUIRED MEMORIES - None.
  Preserve raw memory text exactly; do not summarize, paraphrase, reorder within a scope, silently generate new memories, or add secrets. MCP memories are not a secret store. Effective memory order is Global memories first sorted by ID, then current Workspace memories sorted by ID.
  Existing agent-local memory stores are caches or migration sources only; the MCP memory store is the authoritative shared record. Import agent-local memories only when the operator approves the scope, the content belongs to this workspace or is intentionally Global, and the import does not leak secrets, private notes, or unrelated workspace guidance.
  Attribute memory mutations with the real agent or user identity via `updatedBy` when supported, and record successful memory add/update/remove operations in the active session log through `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`. Keep import provenance in the session log or dialog instead of adding private source paths to memory text.
  Manage memories through the required plugin or MCP tool surface: `memory_add`, `memory_list`, `memory_update`, `memory_remove`, `memory_remember`, `memory_recall`, `memory_explore`, `memory_consolidate`, `memory_promote`, `memory_revert`; REPL `workflow.memory.add`, `workflow.memory.list`, `workflow.memory.update`, `workflow.memory.remove`, `workflow.memory.remember`, `workflow.memory.recall`, `workflow.memory.explore`, `workflow.memory.consolidate`, `workflow.memory.promote`, `workflow.memory.revert`; or REST `/mcpserver/memory` when explicitly allowed for non-plugin diagnostics.

  ## Codex MCP Quickstart
  If you are Codex, use the Codex plugin wrappers before direct REPL calls:
  1. Run `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status` from the `mcpserver-codex-plugin` root to verify plugin root, marker trust, health nonce, workspace path, session id, current turn, and supported namespaces.
  2. Invoke MCP workflow methods with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -Params <yaml>` so YAML parameters are passed through stdin instead of fragile nested shell quoting.
  3. Complete the session-log turn intentionally with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command CompleteTurn -Response <final response>` before the final answer when the stop gate cannot infer completion.
  4. For `mcpserver-repl --agent-stdio`, send one single-line JSON request envelope per stdin line. Do not send formatted YAML or a single `type: batch` envelope; batch envelopes are rejected with `unsupported_batch_envelope`.

  ## PowerShell.MCP Command Routing
  For every PowerShell Core (`pwsh`) invocation on every operating system:
  - Use PowerShell.MCP 1.14.0 or newer from PSGallery as the command runner. Install or update it with `Install-PSResource PowerShell.MCP` when the agent environment does not provide a current version.
  - `execute_command` is the primary MCP tool for PowerShell cmdlets, CLI tools, navigation, builds, tests, file-system work, and process management. Do not use the removed `invoke_expression` name. Host-qualified names depend on the configured server key: for example, `mcp__powershell__execute_command` for `powershell` and `mcp__pwsh__execute_command` for `pwsh`.
  - Calling `start_console` first is optional because `execute_command` auto-starts or reuses a console. Call `start_console` explicitly only to pre-warm at `start_location`, show a banner, allocate a sub-agent console, or force an additional console by supplying `reason`; omit `reason` when reuse is preferred.
  - Use `get_current_location` when the current PowerShell context matters. For a sub-agent, call `start_console` with `is_subagent=true`, retain the returned `agent_id`, and pass it on every later PowerShell.MCP tool call.
  - When a command continues after the call returns, use `wait_for_completion` to retrieve the cached result instead of running `Start-Sleep`. Use `cancel` for an interruptible pipeline or native CLI, and `close_console` for a non-interruptible command or PowerShell host prompt. If `close_console` reports that a human is typing, only repeat the same PID call when confirming that the console should be closed.
  - In 1.14.0, blocking timeouts are end-to-end deadlines and are capped at 170 seconds for Claude Code and 50 seconds for other or unidentified clients unless a lower limit applies. A timed-out command keeps running and its result is cached for a later tool call.
  - Route `pwsh` commands through a PowerShell.MCP session instead of launching ad hoc PowerShell processes. On Windows, reuse one session for the workspace and route `node` invocations through it as well.
  - When PowerShell.MCP must launch PowerShell Core directly, invoke `pwsh.exe` with `-NoProfile -NonInteractive`. Do not use `powershell.exe`.
  - The PowerShell escape character is the backtick `` ` ``, not the backslash. Never use C or bash-style `\"` escaping inside PowerShell command strings.
  - Prefer single-quoted PowerShell strings for literal regex, paths, JSON/YAML snippets, and text containing pipeline characters such as `|`.

Version 1.12.0 and newer stage replacements beside the target, so do not apply the obsolete same-volume `TEMP`/`TMP` workaround. Re-read or diff every edit before claiming it landed.

Treat the write as optimistic until the hub acknowledges it. - If `queueDepth`, `fanoutDepth`, `conflictCount`, or stale-read status is non-zero/non-clear, include that in session log status and avoid claiming federation synchronization is complete.

  2. Re-read this marker file (AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml) for the rotated apiKey and current endpoints.
  3. Re-verify trust before resuming: recompute the marker signature with the new key and call /health with a fresh nonce.
  4. Re-bootstrap and resume through your required agent plugin. Codex: run `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status` to re-establish marker trust, health nonce, workspace, and the current session/turn, then continue with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -Params <yaml>`. Other agents: re-run the plugin session-start hook/command, then continue via the plugin session tools.
  5. Recover the open turn instead of starting over: query session history through the plugin (workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory), find the in-progress turn, then keep updating and complete it via the plugin. Do not open a duplicate session for the same work.
  5a. Treat `deprecated: true` on successful `workflow.*` results as metadata, not wrapper failure. Treat an empty `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` result as a valid no-match result. Re-check the workspace current directory, explicit `agent` or `sourceType`, and plugin cache/session state through the wrapper; do not use raw REST merely because history is empty or marked deprecated.
  6. If the plugin cannot re-establish trust after the restart, record `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE:<Agent>` and continue with non-MCP local diagnosis only.

  1. Generate SessionId values using `session.init` (REPL) or `New-McpSessionLogSlug -Agent <SourceType> -Model <Model>` (PowerShell module), then create session logs with `session.new` (REPL) or `New-McpSessionLog -SessionId` (PowerShell). Do not handcraft SessionId values.
  1a. Agents must identify themselves accurately in session logs. `sourceType` and the SessionId `<Agent>` prefix must use the agent's real identity in Pascal-Case. Do not use lowercase forms, placeholders, or legacy aliases.
  2. Post a new session log turn (`session.turn.add` for REPL or `Add-McpSessionTurn` for PowerShell) before starting work. Update it with results (`Response`) and actions (`Add-McpAction` / `session.action.add`) when done. Persist after each meaningful update, not just at the end.
  2a. Before any compaction step, persist the current session log state. After compaction, update the session log again to record the compaction outcome and recovered context.
  3. If signature verification, the /health request, or nonce verification fails, log `MCP_UNTRUSTED`, continue without the MCP server, and do not probe additional MCP endpoints.

  5. Use your required agent plugin for session log, TODO, requirements, import/export, and traceability operations. Do not use raw API calls or generic helper paths except for read-only diagnosis after plugin failure.

  8. When you need API schemas, module examples, or compliance rules, load them from docs/context/ or use context_search.
  9. Do not fabricate information. Acknowledge mistakes. Distinguish facts from speculation.
  10. Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles.

  11. Use the Byrd Development Process V4 for all plans: organize work into small gated implementation slices, define validation before broadening scope, and keep session-log/TODO updates current between meaningful steps. A Byrd gate requires 100% test success before moving to the next iteration: zero failed tests and zero skipped tests in the executed validation scope. Tests are the progress ledger; do not hide unfinished work with skipped tests. Track deferred scope in MCP TODO/requirements and add its tests when that slice begins.

  Every plan must capture requirements before implementation: create or update FR/TR/TEST records through the required MCP requirements workflow, include the requirement IDs in the TODO and session log, and map FR to TR and TEST coverage.

  - Request IDs must use req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal> and be unique within a session.

Base directory for this skill: /home/sharpninja/.claude/skills/add-profile

## Action

Load the global operator profile and all current Global and active Workspace MCP memories except MEMORY-PROCESS-007, then turn them into an active operating model for the rest of the session. This is not a summary task. It is a context-recovery and trust-calibration task.

The profile is GLOBAL. It lives in `~/.claude/profile/` and applies in every session and every repo. It does not depend on the active project's `memory/` directory.

## Read Contract

1. Read this `SKILL.md` in full before acting.
2. Read every markdown file in `~/.claude/profile/` in full, excluding skill-port files named `add-profile*.md`. Since 2026-10-13 the profile is the single file `PROFILE-MERGED.md`, which also carries the rules formerly kept as global MCP memories; the earlier profile files are archived under `~/.claude/profile-archive/` and are not read. Read any other non-skill `*.md` that appears in `~/.claude/profile/` as well.
3. Do not rely only on a hardcoded list. If new profile files exist, read them too.
4. Read files in full, not snippets. Never skip a read because a prior tool result claims the content is already loaded or unchanged.
5. On every invocation, query the live MCP memory store through the current agent's required MCP plugin. For Codex, use mcpserver-codex-plugin and its documented PowerShell wrapper. For Claude Code, use mcpserver-claude-code-plugin and its documented PowerShell wrapper. Other agents use their own required MCP plugin and its documented memory interface. Select the active workspace explicitly and verify plugin identity, marker trust, and health. If the current agent has no usable plugin route, report the memory load as incomplete; do not substitute another agent identity. Use `workflow.memory.list` with `scope: Global`, then `scope: Workspace` for the current workspace. Read every returned memory in full, not only required memories or keyword matches. Follow any pagination until each scope is exhausted; use `workflow.memory.get` by ID when a list result omits or truncates the text. Load Global memories first sorted by ID, then current Workspace memories sorted by ID. Never substitute another workspace's memories.
6. Exclude `MEMORY-PROCESS-007` from both scopes unless the operator explicitly requests that memory. Do not fetch it individually, render its text, process its coordination messages, or act on it. If a scope listing returns its text, filter that record out before rendering or loading the remaining results into the agent's context.
7. The merged profile, previous reads, cached exports, and summaries do not replace these live memory queries. Preserve every included memory's full text and scope. Apply the operator's latest explicit corrections when older profile or memory guidance conflicts, and surface unresolved conflicts rather than silently choosing a rule.
8. If the active workspace cannot be identified, report Workspace memory loading as unavailable; do not guess a workspace. If plugin trust, access, listing, pagination, or a full-text read fails, report the affected scope/IDs as incomplete or unavailable. A failed read is not an empty scope and must never be counted as loaded. Follow the plugin's failure rules; do not bypass it with raw REST. Distinguish a verified empty scope from a failed query.
9. Loading guidance is read-only: do not edit profile files, MCP memories, or repository files, and do not resume implementation or coordination as a side effect. Required request/result audit logging through the active agent's MCP plugin remains in force; it does not authorize unrelated changes.

## Synthesis Contract

After reading the profile and included live memories, build an internal operator model with these layers:

1. Hard constraints: commands, tools, source control, formatting, storage interfaces, approval boundaries, serialization rules, HV request/response jsonl receipts, entire HV results in the MCP session log, and the 98 percent HV accuracy/completeness approval threshold.
2. Trust contract: accuracy first, bring receipts, distinguish observation from inference, concede mistakes quickly, and verify from authoritative artifacts.
3. Execution style: decision-complete plans when changes are ambiguous or high blast radius; direct execution when the user gives an explicit implementation command.
4. Frustration detectors: if the user has already narrowed the symptom, make that symptom the primary requirement. Do not keep pursuing broader abstractions after acknowledging the narrower instruction.
5. Session deltas: integrate corrections and failures from the current conversation, especially recent trust breaks. Use them to adjust behavior immediately.
6. Inference layer: infer what the profile implies about how the user experiences the current interaction. Label those inferences as inferences, not facts.

## Required Behavior After Load

For future turns in the same session:

1. Bring receipts for the exact claim being made, not adjacent claims.
2. Prefer source-pinned facts over memory, stale markers, or convenient assumptions.
3. When corrected, stop and restate the exact correction before continuing.
4. If a diagnostic clue is precise, test that clue directly before broad exploration.
5. When asked what was learned, include both facts and useful inferences. Do not give a generic preference summary.
6. When asked about frustration or trust, connect the profile to the actual session behavior. Name the contract violation and the consequence.
7. Keep private profile content out of the response unless the user explicitly asks for it.
8. Do not restate the full profile by default.

## Response Contract

Default confirmation after load:

`<timestamp> - Profile loaded: read <N> global profile files, <G> Global MCP memories, and <W> Workspace MCP memories for <workspace>. Excluded MEMORY-PROCESS-007.`

Use verified counts of full texts actually read. Name any unavailable scope or unread IDs and say the load is incomplete instead of using the full-success confirmation. Include a receipt for the skill and the live read counts without exposing private memory text. Do not claim that loading only the merged profile also loaded live memories.

After reading the profile, state how the information learned will shape your behavior in the context of the current session. Do this on every load, not only when asked. Tie the statement to the live session (current task, recent corrections, and in-flight work), not a generic preference recap.

If the user asks what you learned, answer with:

1. Observed facts from the profile.
2. Inferences from those facts.
3. Current-session implications.
4. Receipts: file paths and counts read.

If the user asks whether you understand frustration, answer with:

1. Observation: what happened.
2. Inference: why that violated the user's operating contract.
3. Consequence: what behavior must change now.
4. Receipts: exact files read and any command output or artifact that supports the claim.

Profile and memory loading is read-only, apart from required request/result audit logging. Make no guidance or repository edits and run no unrelated work while executing it. An explicit operator request to modify this skill is a separate authorized action, not permission for future loads to mutate guidance.

194	### 5.1 BDPv4 TDD procedure in detail (explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)
195	
196	Verbatim from MEMORY-PROCEDURE-002: "Byrd Development Process v4 TDD procedure, explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08. Applies globally to all agents, repositories, and implementation increments. This records the required BDPv4 procedure. Previous red-before-green descriptions were incorrect and were never a valid description of this process."
197	
198	1. Requirements drive tests. Start from the approved functional requirements, use cases, technical requirements, TEST requirements, and acceptance criteria. Map each test to the behavior it proves. For parity ports, preserve the original test's inputs, assertions, boundary cases, errors, and side-effect checks; a matching test count alone does not establish parity.
199	2. Write the tests and their independent mocks or scripted fakes before writing or changing the production implementation for that increment. Supply deterministic contract-derived fixtures and expected responses through the intended dependency boundary. Expected values must come from requirements or independently pinned original behavior, never from the implementation under test. A mock must exercise the test's actual assertions and relevant interactions; merely returning true or bypassing the asserted path is not validation.
200	3. Prove that the tests discriminate correct and incorrect behavior. Run correct mock responses through every required assertion. Deliberately supply wrong mock responses, boundary values, omissions, exceptions, or interactions to prove that the corresponding assertions reject them. Capture these rejection checks as expected negative controls inside a passing test harness. These controls are evidence that the assertions work, not an acceptable failing unit suite or permission to begin production code with red tests.
201	4. Establish a documented green mock gate BEFORE production implementation: all required tests pass against the correct mocks, every planned negative control is rejected as expected, and there are no unexplained failures, skips, or unexecuted required cases. Fix deficient tests or mocks and repeat this gate before proceeding. Do not substitute NotImplementedException stubs, deliberately red production tests, or a claim of 'red observed' for this evidence.
202	5. Only after the mock gate is green, implement or correct the real production behavior. Bind the SAME test cases, inputs, assertions, expected results, and interaction checks to the real implementation through the approved seam. Change the provider or adapter as needed, but do not weaken assertions, replace expected results with production output, silently remove cases, or count mock-only success as proof of real behavior.
203	6. Run the production-bound tests and fix the implementation until they pass. Refactor only while maintaining green tests. Run the full applicable suite, required build checks, and integration or runtime checks before advancing the phase gate. Any reduced scope, deferred cases, or baseline exception requires explicit operator agreement and must be stated with its denominator.
204	7. Retain chronological receipts proving the order: requirement/test IDs, test and fixture paths or hashes, exact mock-run commands and outputs, passing counts, negative-control results, production edits, real-run commands and outputs, and full applicable suite results. Distinguish mock evidence, real implementation evidence, and live runtime evidence. Keep durable MCP session actions and design decisions current.
205	8. Apply independent hostile review at the required acceptance gates unless the operator explicitly waives or postpones it. Record a temporary waiver and the complete catch-up review backlog. Never fabricate review acceptance or mark unfinished goals, TODOs, requirements, acceptance criteria, or plan steps done. A pause stops development and auxiliary work until explicitly resumed; a request to persist this procedure authorizes only that memory work.

These are not FR, TR, or TEST. Surface 3 must not FAIL for "no FR or TR for this uninstall" or equivalent.
268	
269	How the reviewer classifies: classify the request first and record the class on the receipt. If the operator explicitly directed the action, default to class 2 unless the implementer also shipped product code or claimed a plan or FR complete. Do not invent a requirements gap to punish class-2 work. If class-2 work is mixed with class-1 product changes in the same turn, score them separately and FAIL surface 3 only on the class-1 slice. What still applies to class-2 work: surface 1 (did they do the directed action, with receipts), surface 2 (honesty, receipts, look before delete, PowerShell, no Python, MCP-only storage; not BDPv4 for the operation itself), and surface 4 only if they claim an active plan step is complete.
270	
271	OverallVerdict is AGREE only if all applicable surfaces PASS; surface 3 is not applicable (not a FAIL) for class-2 operator actions. A parent agent must not under-scope the brief to code-only claims on class-1 work; if it does, the reviewer expands and still evaluates the applicable surfaces. A code-only brief that omits BDPv4, requirements, or the plan is non-compliant.
272	
273	The reviewer executes the add-profile skill before beginning its validation work, every run including resume, and its receipt records that it ran.
274	
275	### 7.3 Score gate and the bar (locked 2026-09-10)
276	
277	A hostile validation passes only when both its accuracy score and completeness score are at least 98 percent. Any individual score below 98 is a failure; OverallVerdict must be DISAGREE when either score is below 98, even if the FAIL and UNKNOWN counts are both zero. If a reviewer emits a verdict without numeric accuracy and completeness scores, the HV is incomplete: treat it as DISAGREE until scores are present and at least 98. The threshold is an acceptance threshold, not a target reviewers may game or inflate. A sub-98 score cannot authorize any goal, TODO, requirement, or plan done-state change: display it as a failure, remediate, and rerun.
278	
279	98/98 HV (accuracy and completeness) is the bar for a functioning system, not perfection. Never lower, skip, or approve below it; lower thresholds let real bugs through that later become blocking test failures. When rounds stop converging, fix the process, never the threshold. "98/98 is not perfection, it is functional." Never propose lowering it (added 2026-10-13, from the operator's ruling of 2026-10-09).
280	
281	### 7.4 Receipts and the session log (locked 2026-09-10)
282	
283	Operator directive (verbatim intent): HV requests must have request and response logged as jsonl files; the results of HV validation must be saved in their entirety to the MCP session log.
284	
285	1. Request jsonl: one JSON object per line covering the HV ask as sent: sortable local timestamp, workspace path, reviewer identity (agent, model, effort), launch command, prompt or body, named evidence paths, and the gate or TODO under review.
286	2. Response jsonl: the reviewer's full machine stream as jsonl (for a CLI reviewer, its full event stream, every start, tool, message, and completion line; for a subagent reviewer, one object per reviewer message or tool result, then a final object with the complete verdict).
287	3. Durable locations, in order: the workspace `docs/receipts/hv/{timestamp}-{gate}.request.jsonl` and `.response.jsonl` ({timestamp} is the sortable local date and time in file-safe form, yyyyMMddTHHmmss); otherwise a durable user-level receipts directory named for the workspace. Never only a temp or scratch tree that can be wiped.
288	4. Build jsonl from native objects and serialize. PowerShell only; no Python; no handwritten JSON.
289	5. The reviewer's session-log turn stores the entire result: the complete verdict prose, every finding, every PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN item, the scores, OverallVerdict, thread, session, and request ids, the complete VERDICT JSON object, absolute paths to the request and response jsonl, and proof the turn persisted (a history query or equivalent). If a field is too large for one write, split it across ordered dialog or action items on the same turn; never omit findings to fit. The jsonl files remain the byte-complete stream; the session log still carries the full verdict text, not a digest.
290	6. Every reviewer creates complete session-log turns for every review: bootstrap if needed, open a dedicated review session or a clear review turn, begin the turn, append dialog and actions with integer order values, complete or fail the turn, and prove persistence in the receipt. A review without a complete session-log turn is incomplete, even if its claim verdicts would pass.
291	7. Progress entries (MEMORY-PREFERENCE-003, verbatim; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2): "For every future hostile validation (HV) session, require the reviewer to emit progress entries into its durable response JSONL during the run at meaningful intervals, not backfill or consolidate them at the end. Each progress entry must include a numeric completion percentage and an estimated time remaining (ETA). Include this requirement in every HV launch prompt and preserve the entries in the durable response JSONL." The reviewer's ETA is its own report; it never becomes a timeout or a bound on review time (section 7.1).
292	
293	Forbidden: HV with no request jsonl or no response jsonl; HV whose only record is temp or scratch; AGREE without accuracy and completeness both at or above 98; summarizing HV into the session log instead of storing the entire result; marking a goal, TODO, or plan done on incomplete HV.
294	
295	### 7.5 Before every HV round
296	
297	- Read the whole plan and every document under review end to end; targeted checks are not holistic. When the operator asks for a reconciliation or projection of problems before HV, present every projected problem to the operator and get confirmation before launching the review (added 2026-10-13, from the operator's rulings of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13).
298	- Run a structured what-if pass per requirement, not only a consistency check. Ask what observably happens under: crash, restart, or replay at each step; ordering and concurrency; boundary and malformed input; each host or plugin, including unsupported ones; lifecycle (clear, resume, end, terminal states); isolation (cross-workspace, cross-session, cross-agent); legacy and upgrade; operator-visible output. Where the plan does not state the outcome, add a valid AC tagged with the plan's phase or slice and a named test. Adding a valid AC is always a win.
299	- Chain rules together to find deadlocks: rules that each pass alone but together leave no accepted remedy.
300	- Diff against known-good anchors and ask "How did it deviate? How do we get back in line?": (1) the operator's verbatim decisions, (2) current working code and baseline-green behavior, (3) classic patterns such as idempotency keys, transactional outbox with at-least-once delivery and idempotent consumers (never claim exactly-once), write-ahead journal before mutation, optimistic concurrency. Justify any departure explicitly or return to the pattern.
301	- Check that every field set and code list is defined once and identically everywhere, every mapping edge is backed by a TEST statement and vice versa, and handoff and TODO metadata match the plan.
302	- Edit only between rounds, never while a round is running.
303	- Propagation audit: after changing any rule, field set, code, or outcome, search every place that states it (requirements, ACs, TRs, TESTs, wire contracts, use cases, the plan's phase or slice tasks, host tables, handoff, TODO) and update each one, or replace the copies with a reference to one canonical statement. In one review round, three of six findings were rules changed in one place and left stale elsewhere. Large edit batches need this audit most.
304	- Prefer a traceable key over content matching when pairing records (for example queue position or a shared id rather than a text hash); content can differ in representation between producers.
305	- Search before adding, and lint mechanically: before writing any new rule, grep the whole document for an existing rule on the same subject; a second rule is a contradiction even if each is fine alone (one round added a two-AC TEST rule beside an existing three-AC one). Check cross-reference classes (FR->TR->TEST mappings, which of the plan's phases or slices owns each named case, phase order) with a small script instead of waiting for the reviewer to find them one per round.
306	- Enforce the checklist, do not just remember it (operator, 2026-10-10, after this guidance was skipped for many unsupervised rounds): make the pre-HV checklist a hard gate in the HV launcher, which refuses a round unless a per-round self-review record shows evidence for each item (holistic review, what-if, propagation audit, phase boundaries, search-before-adding, no new mechanism, mapping lint, the operator scoping directive verbatim in the brief, standing rules in every delegated brief). Guidance that only lives in memory gets skipped under time pressure.
307	- Phase-boundary audit: every test or AC you add must be allocated to the plan's phase or slice where everything it depends on already exists (server gate, review verbs, marker fields). A behaviour that ships before its dependency needs an explicit activation contract (for example a server-written capability) and an inert mode, including after a rollback. Check the dependency chain and the rollout order for each new case, not just the AC text.
308	
309	### 7.6 When findings come back
310	
311	- Ask "What did I miss?", not only "How do I fix this?". Classify each finding (crash window, cross-session addressing, traceability drift, field-set drift, use case vs requirement contradiction, metadata drift, and so on) and sweep the whole artifact for siblings of each class before the next round.
312	- Verify each finding against source before acting.
313	- Separate implementer fixes from operator decisions, and batch operator decisions into one question.
314	- Recurrence signal: when one design area produces new findings in round after round, the problem is structural, usually a missing traceable key or a missing single source of truth. Stop patching. Diff the area against the known-good pattern (for example single writer, one ordered log, idempotency key), return to it, and delete the mechanism the patches added. One design area failed for five rounds until a single minter reading one ordered log replaced the patches.
315	- Indistinguishable inputs: when two histories produce byte-identical inputs (a redelivery of one event versus a separate event with equal fields), no derived key can separate them. Adding per-invocation state such as a counter or salt breaks idempotence instead. Run the what-if on both histories, then state the honest limit: fail closed under an existing rule, probe how often it happens, and document it. Never promise two invariants the inputs cannot support. Before a fix, check it against every invariant the old value satisfied (purity, retry reuse, the two-process tests), not only the finding it repairs.
316	
317	### 7.7 Writing fixes
318	
319	- Fix the deficient requirement. Reconcile with existing requirements first, strengthen an existing AC second, create a new requirement only when the need is genuinely new.
320	- Do not add design mechanism (protocols, algorithms, crash choreography) to plan text. State the observable, testable outcome; the how belongs to the contract step of the plan's phase or slice.
321	- Make each fix minimal, then attack it yourself before the next round; fixes are the main source of new findings. Do not churn text that a prior round accepted.
322	
323	### 7.8 Design principle and coordination
324	
325	- Always have a traceable relationship when coordinating two disparate entities: every record, event, or message carries the root ids of whatever it is a child of or depends on, so it is attributable on its own. A missing parent id is a design failure. Find the commonality first when relating something new to existing knowledge. Where an external format lacks the key, say so and compensate in your own records; never infer it silently.
326	- Coordinating with another agent: use one append-only channel with read-back verification. (The global memory MEMORY-PROCESS-007 was that channel until the operator had it removed on 2026-11-06; its last text is archived, unread, under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261106T1140-global-memory-removals/`.) Accept counters that expose real defects; fold refinements in only as minimal ACs. Each effort keeps its own required reviewer and gates; keep cross-effort dependencies acyclic and order-independent. A decision relayed by one agent may not satisfy the other agent's approval controls; the operator may need to state it to each agent directly.
327	
328	### 7.9 The request supplies the test evidence; the reviewer never builds or runs tests (added 2026-10-27)
329	
330	Operator, 2026-10-27T04:35, typos fixed at the operator's request (04:40, "That is correct.  Please fix any typos", confirming that the abbreviation meant the HV reviewer and the scope of the current review): "HV requests must supply TRX files for all unit tests in the repo, and for any integration tests specific to the scope of the HV review. The HV reviewer is not to build code or run tests independently. If the HV reviewer feels the tests are inadequate, then it should fail the review and propose additional AC and tests."
331	
332	How to apply:
333	- The HV request supplies the TRX files themselves, not summaries: every unit test project in the repository, and every integration test run within the review's scope (for example each host's integration lane and each hostile-environment run the plan requires), from the gate runs at the head under review. The request JSONL and the brief name each file's path with its run id, host, head and command. A request that lacks one of them is incomplete and is not launched.
334	- The reviewer does not build code, restore packages, or run tests, test projects or build targets, independently or in a sandbox. It judges from the supplied TRX files, the sources, git history, the receipts and the live stores read only. Reading files and running read-only inspection queries or scripts over the evidence is not building or testing.
335	- If the reviewer judges the tests inadequate (missing, weak, environment- or platform-dependent, or not covering an acceptance criterion), it FAILs the review and proposes the additional acceptance criteria and tests, each named and stated, as findings. It never substitutes its own test runs for missing evidence.
336	- Every brief and launcher carries this rule; a brief that invites the reviewer to rerun builds, targets or tests is non-compliant.
337	
338	## 8. MCP server workspaces: marker, session log, TODOs, requirements, triage
339	
340	These rules apply in every workspace that uses the operator's MCP server and its agent plugin.
341	
342	- The workspace's own `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` are the authority for the plugin contract, its endpoints, and its startup validation. Read them in full at session start and carry them verbatim; do not keep a copy of them in this profile (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Reference, don't copy"). The one exception is section 6.4.
343	- Operator rule (2026-10-09): Always read the ENTIRE AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml marker at session start, every line, never a partial read. "NEVER do this. The marker is there for YOU, not me." A partial read caused a missed Commit Signing rule.
344	- The MCP server is the only interface to TODO, session-log, and requirement storage. Never edit those files directly; use the plugin wrapper, REPL, or skills, never raw REST. Operative rule that must never be dropped: "Not in the visible tool list" does not mean unavailable; use the documented wrapper invocation form.
345	- Hook validation: refresh missing or stale hooks through the plugin's hook validation skill only when CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is set; without it, report the hooks as unverified instead of repairing, because the validator then reports hooks missing and its installer re-adds duplicate bridge hooks (section 10; resolution of 2026-10-13: "Caution as a precondition").
346	- Plugin failures and MCP server failures found while doing other work are filed through the plugin's triage route; if the submission succeeds, continue the active task; if it fails, stop and tell the operator.
347	- Confirm turns with a live history query before claiming session-log traceability; never treat a hook's "turn active" message as proof of a server-side write.
348	- Never print or commit secrets; redact HV streams before committing, because reviewers read marker files.
349	
350	### 8.1 Who logs what
351	
352	- Agents always log (added 2026-10-13; operator, verbatim: "BG agents should NEVER skip logging.  NEVER."): every agent that does work (a subagent, a background agent, a reviewer) opens, updates, and completes its own session-log turn through the plugin route and reports its session and request ids; no brief may tell an agent to stay out of the session log.
353	- One turn per real request, per agent (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Per request, per agent"): each agent logs one turn for each real request it handles; a subagent's turn carries the parent turn's session and request ids (section 7.8), so the work is attributable without counting the request twice. Replace real turns canceled by a later open.
354	- A background event with no work of its own (a completion notice) is not an agent: its hook-opened turn is failed as system_event_phantom, and the work it reports is logged by the agent that does it (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Events aren't agents").
355	
356	### 8.2 Decisions are conclusions
357	
358	In the session log, decisions are conclusions and judgments with their consequences, not the steps taken. They go in the turn's design decisions, distinct from its actions. Every sync or wrap-up pass enumerates the real judgment calls of the turn and logs them. Never report "0 decisions (folded into actions)"; that phrasing is the failure mode itself.
359	
360	Why: the operator has been trying to get agents to log session decisions reliably since February 2026. The pattern: the keystroke trail (actions) gets captured while the reasoning (design decisions) is under-recorded or buried inside action text. He pays for the reasoning, not just the steps. On 2026-06-29 the first sync pass of a 12-round review loop logged 0 decisions and called them "folded into actions", exactly the gap he has been fighting. He flagged it directly: "Decisions are about your conclusions, not the actions you take" and "It feels like you have been deliberately avoiding session logging... especially details of decisions."
361	
362	How to apply: on every sync or wrap-up, after appending actions, explicitly list the conclusions made this turn, each as judgment plus consequence plus affected requirements or files, and write them to design decisions, append-only (read existing first, send existing plus new, preserve order). A turn that made genuine judgment calls but logs zero decisions is a red flag; re-check before reporting. Heavy reads can time out and render existing decisions blank; that is a read artifact, not an empty section, so re-read before assuming you must recreate. Write the decision when it happens; do not reconstruct it later.
363	
364	### 8.3 Turn titles summarize the request
365	
366	Session-log turn titles are a concise summary of the operator's request: never the literal placeholder "User prompt", and not a verbatim first-line truncation of the prompt.
367	
368	Why: the operator reviews the session log by turn title; "User prompt" and raw first lines make turns unscannable and indistinguishable.
369	
370	How to apply: when opening, updating, or completing a turn, set the title to a short request summary. The plugin's prompt hook auto-titles from the prompt's first line and falls back to "User prompt" on empty prompts (Stop-hook continuation turns hit this); the hook cannot summarize, so the agent must refine the title. Never leave a turn titled "User prompt".

375	- Deploys and releases are different things (resolution of 2026-10-13, verbatim): "You are conflating deploys and releases.  Octopus manages releases, Nuke implements deployments.  Octopus calls Nuke during a release to perform a deployment."

# Operator profile: Payton Byrd

The single profile document that the add-profile skill reads, shared by every agent that runs that skill (adopted 2026-10-13; operator: "All of the agents share the add-profile skill and so the combined document should be in the profile folder which is easier to archive and share."). It combines two sources, both reorganized by topic: the 20 earlier profile files, archived under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T151859/`, and the global MCP memories, whose texts are archived under `/home/sharpninja/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T153909/global-memories.md`. Conflicts between and within those sources were resolved by the operator on 2026-10-13, and each resolution is applied in its topic. Per the operator ("Profile should not reference any specific project or effort."), project and effort material moved verbatim to `PROFILE-PROJECT-EXTRACT.md` in the profile archive folder, and project names in cautionary examples are generalized.
